subject: A8A268456D19E3888627BDEB1F3317E5
introduction: “Believe not every speaker, trust not in every newcomer.” A new religion attracts imitators, and the Bábí community of the 1850s and 1860s saw many: after the Báb’s martyrdom a number of people claimed revelation or divinity, and others gathered followers around prophecies and secret knowledge. These readings are Bahá’u’lláh’s and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s response. They give tests: conduct, motive, proof, and whether the person seeks wealth or following. They give one fixed safeguard, that no one may claim a direct Revelation from God “ere the expiration of a full thousand years.” They show the Central Figures themselves refusing titles pressed upon them. And they ask that those who make such claims be treated kindly and welcomed back if they return. Every scripture has had to face the same problem, and the parallels are close: “try the spirits,” wolves in sheep’s clothing, the tests of a prophet in Deuteronomy and Jeremiah, Simon the sorcerer, the Qur’án on one who “saith: I am inspired, when he is not.” Peter, Paul, John the Baptist and an angel all refuse worship. Moses’s wish that all the people were prophets, and Hobbes’s scepticism about any private revelation, raise the question of where personal inspiration stands.
questions: “Believe not every speaker.” What tests do the readings and the parallel scriptures give for a claim to spiritual authority? Which could you apply without special knowledge?
Several readings point to money and following as signs. Why are motive and conduct treated as evidence about the truth of a claim?
The thousand-year safeguard rules out even a claimant who brings “all the verses.” What does a community gain from so definite a rule, and what would it risk without it?
Peter, Paul, an angel, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá all refuse honours offered them. What does that refusal tell you about how real authority behaves?
Moses wished “that all the Lord’s people were prophets.” What room do the readings leave for personal insight and inspiration, short of a claim to authority?
“Do not oppose the Qadiyanis. Deal with them kindly.” How should one treat a person whose claim one believes to be false, and that person’s followers?

outside.why: “Believe not every speaker, trust not in every newcomer.” John, in nearly the same words: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.
Paul keeps both halves of the duty in three short sentences: quench not the Spirit. Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

When the Proof cannot be consulted, “act according to what God hath revealed in the Book.” The Bereans tested even an apostle that way: they searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
An unsigned letter of “false and fabricated statements.” The Qur’án: woe be unto those who write the Scripture with their hands and then say, “This is from Allah.”
“The writings of such fraudulent souls serve as their own exposure.” Jesus: ye shall know them by their fruits.
Some make the praise of God “a snare for people.” Jesus: ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer.

One who “claimed divine revelation and wrongfully taken people’s” wealth. Micah: the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us?
The Qur’án: many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of mankind wantonly and debar men from the way of Allah.
Simon the sorcerer thought spiritual power could be bought, and was told: thy money perish with thee.
“Every transgressor adorneth himself with the vesture of piety.” Paul: Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
“The wolves clothe themselves with the shepherd’s garment.” Jesus: beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing.
“Thieves show themselves in the form of watchmen.” Jesus: he that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.
One “claims association with Thee” and dishonours it. Jesus: not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord.
In days of glory all claim to love; “that claim depends upon another test.” The seed on stony ground: when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.
No one is to be excused for following some individual as “a manifest mirror.” Paul bound even himself: though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you, let him be accursed.

Whoever claims a Revelation before a thousand years “is assuredly a lying impostor.” Deuteronomy: the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, shall die.

Other scriptures have set a limit on later claims too. The Qur’án: he is the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. Bahá’u’lláh’s limit is a period of time, after which another may come. What difference does it make to believers whether the door is closed or closed for a season?

Even one who came “with all the verses” within the thousand years is not to be accepted. The warning that closes the New Testament: if any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book.
Not signs and not eloquence are the test. Jesus: there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; believe it not.
“Before the passing of a thousand years, any claim is forbidden.” Deuteronomy on a prophet whose sign comes true but whose message leads away: thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet.

An unknown person “laid claim, and some heedless ones were attracted,” and then returned. Gamaliel recalls such a case: Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.
To claim that station is to have “fabricated a lie against God.” Jeremiah: I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.

Otherwise “the Cause of God would be corrupted.” Moses, told that two men were prophesying without leave, refused to stop them: would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets! What is the difference between the inspiration Moses welcomes and the claim the reading forbids?
“Think not that Revelation is such that any soul may, whenever it pleaseth, manifest itself.” Hebrews: no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God.
“We beseech God to guide him to recant; if he repents” he is forgiven. Paul: if a man be overtaken in a fault, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.

“Whosoever layeth claim to a Cause, he is a lying impostor.” The Qur’án: who is guilty of more wrong than he who forgeth a lie against Allah, or saith: I am inspired, when he is not inspired in aught?
One who came “with all the books in the world” and spoke otherwise than God willed. Micaiah, pressed to agree with four hundred court prophets: what the Lord saith unto me, that will I speak.
“They have taken fancy for certainty.” Ezekiel: woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!
Knowledge claimed “without clear proof.” Jeremiah: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.
People ignorant of the Cause’s foundation “are now occupied with leading souls astray.” Jesus: they be blind leaders of the blind.
“Believe not every speaker … nor hearken unto every claimant.” Proverbs: the simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.
“Whosoever claimeth for himself a station, he is a liar.” Simon of Samaria: giving out that himself was some great one: to whom they all gave heed, saying, This man is the great power of God.

A believer may attain a deeper understanding than the learned can bear; the reading weighs what follows from that. Hobbes on any private claim to revelation: to say he hath spoken to him in a Dream, is no more then to say he dreamed that God spake to him. What standing do the readings give to personal insight, and what do they withhold from it?
Some “summon the people to the dawning-place of vain imaginings.” They find hearers, as Isaiah knew: which say to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things.
“Those who worship their own desires and imagine they worship their Ancient Lord.” The Qur’án: hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god?
They are “worshippers of idols, though they perceive it not.” The psalm: they that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.
One who “laid claim to divine authority of his own accord.” Korah to Moses: ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them.
Those who “usurped the station of Truth in the name of Truth.” Paul: so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.
“They call upon God with their tongues,” and turn back at the first command they dislike. Isaiah: with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me.
Flattery and sweet speech lead souls astray. Jeremiah: the prophets prophesy falsely; and my people love to have it so.
Jesus: woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
“The firefly hath laid claim to the station of the sun.” Shakespeare: man, proud man, drest in a little brief authority, most ignorant of what he’s most assured.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá “would never barter servitude at the Sacred Threshold for the sovereignty of both worlds.” Paul: made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant.
John the Baptist, asked who he was: I am not the Christ, but I am sent before him. He must increase, but I must decrease.

The reading recalls early believers who cried “I am God” in ecstasy, and distinguishes that from a claim to authority. Whitman: divine am I inside and out. Is a cry of rapture a claim? What turns the one into the other?
“Some have said that He hath claimed divinity.” The Qur’án has its Prophet say: I am only a mortal like you. My Lord inspireth in me that your God is only One God.
The Báb, under examination: “whoever claims specific deputyship … is a false pretender.” Paul and Barnabas, hailed as gods at Lystra, rent their clothes: we also are men of like passions with you.
Peter, when Cornelius fell at his feet: stand up; I myself also am a man.
And an angel, when John fell down to worship: see thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant.
A boy is being educated to be the promised one. “God must select the Promised One, not men.” Samuel, shown Jesse’s tall eldest son: the Lord seeth not as man seeth.
A teacher claimed authorship of what was not his. Jesus: be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master.
Many claimed divinity in the Islamic era. “What did they gain?” Gamaliel’s test of time: if this work be of men, it will come to nought.

Some foretell events they themselves arrange. Deuteronomy’s plain test, which this trick is designed to pass: if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken.
“In all ages there have been such false souls.” Peter: there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you.
As soon as there was security, “certain ignorant ones in every city laid claim to divinity.” John: even now are there many antichrists. They went out from us, but they were not of us.
A people who thought themselves the saved sect, through such imaginings, came to kill the One they awaited. Jesus: had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me.
“They cling to a name … while turning away from Him Who brought it into being.” Jesus: search the scriptures; they are they which testify of me. And ye will not come to me.
“Beware lest you follow every remote calf.” Paul: after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears.
False claimants “shall appear in every land.” Paul’s farewell at Ephesus: of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
“I counsel all … to guard themselves against false pretenders.” Ezekiel: if the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet, his blood will I require.
“Follow not those unto whom God hath given no authority.” Jesus: my sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
A prayer to “remain unmoved by the perplexing suggestions” of such people. Paul: that we be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine.
“Cause me … to be so steadfast in Thy love.” Paul: be ye stedfast, unmoveable.
“Do not oppose the Qadiyanis. Deal with them kindly.” Paul: be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
Teach him “with perfect love and kindness.” Paul: in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves.

Those who claimed knowledge have lost, “except they repent and return unto the Forgiving.” The father of the prodigal: when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran.

shortfall: Many of the 76 readings repeat one warning in nearly the same words (“false claimants have appeared and will appear”), and several concern particular persons and episodes in Bábí and Bahá’í history. The guide is read with 66 outside quotations, each placed where it adds a test, a parallel case or a question; none was added only to reach the number.

acts-theudas-boasting-himself-to-be-some.text: For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought

thessalonians-shewing-himself-that-he-is.text: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God

deuteronomy-prophet-which-shall-presume.text: But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die

hebrews-no-man-taketh-this-honour.text: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron

matthew-devour-widows-houses.text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation

john-climbeth-up-some-other-way.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber

quran-who-saith-i-am-inspired.text: Who is guilty of more wrong than he who forgeth a lie against Allah, or saith: I am inspired, when he is not inspired in aught; and who saith: I will reveal the like of that which Allah hath revealed? If thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers reach the pangs of death and the angels stretch their hands out (saying): Deliver up your souls. This day ye are awarded doom of degradation for that ye spake concerning Allah other than the truth, and used to scorn His portents.

john-epistle-many-antichrists.text: Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time. They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us
